note:
**The meaning of the verse**
﴿وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ﴾
As for the one who asks, do not drive him away harshly; rather, feed him and meet his need.

And if you have nothing to give, Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلًا مَّيْسُورًا﴾
And if you turn away from giving those you were commanded to give, because you have nothing to give them from, while seeking provision you are waiting for from your Lord, then speak to them with a gentle, kind word, such as making du'a for them to be enriched and given plenty of provision, and promise them that when Allah grants provision from His bounty, you will give them from it.

And He said: ﴿قَوْلٌ مَّعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِّن صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُهَا أَذًى ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمٌ﴾
A good word with which the one who asks is turned away, and forgiveness for any pressing he showed in asking, is better than a sadaqah that the giver follows with hurt and offence.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Ziyad say to the stranger? And why did he wish afterwards that he could take his words back?
2. Uncle Mansour said, "Someone who stands at the door and asks has already had something break inside him before he could ask. So don't you break what is left." What does that mean?
3. All Ziyad had was half a loaf, so what did he say to the old woman? And if we have nothing to give, do we turn away the one who asks harshly? (No; we excuse ourselves to him with a gentle word and make du'a for him, as in the verse: ﴿فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلًا مَّيْسُورًا﴾ (speak to them a gentle word).)

**This week's exercise**
Agree with your child on a kind sentence of apology to say when they are asked for something they cannot give, and practise it together. And prepare together a small bag with water and dates, which they hand with their right hand this week to a worker or someone in need you meet.
